learn.title: Wind Turbine Lifespan & Blade Recycling
learn.intro: Wind turbines last 20-25 years, but blade disposal creates waste. Recycling reduces landfill use and supports circular energy systems, critical for sustainable growth.
learn.c1_text: Modern blades last 20-25 years. Like car tires, wear from weather and rotation necessitates replacement. Aging blades pose landfill risks if not recycled.
learn.c2_text: Blades are often landfilled due to composite materials. Recycling processes like pyrolysis break down resins, recovering 90% of materials for reuse in new products.
learn.c3_text: India aims for 500 GW renewable capacity by 2030. With 30 GW wind installed, blade recycling startups like Attero are pioneering solutions to meet waste targets.
learn.stat2: Global blade waste projected to reach 4 million tons by 2050
learn.stat3: Recycling one blade saves 10 tons of CO2 emissions
learn.stat4: India’s National Policy on Circular Economy (2023) targets 50% waste reduction in renewables

learn.title: Floating Solar Farms on Water
learn.intro: Floating solar reduces water evaporation by 70%, conserving resources while generating clean energy. Ideal for reservoirs and lakes.
learn.c1_text: Floating panels stay cooler (+10% efficiency) and avoid land-use conflicts. A 1 MW plant can save 2.5 million liters of water annually.
learn.c2_text: By shading water, evaporation drops by 70%. In drought-prone regions, this preserves freshwater for agriculture and drinking.
learn.c3_text: India’s first floating solar project in Hyderabad’s Hussain Sagar lake generates 600 kW. The government targets 10 GW floating solar by 2030.
learn.stat2: 1 MW floating solar saves 2.5 million liters water/year
learn.stat4: India’s National Solar Mission includes floating solar in its 2030 plan

learn.title: Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) Technology
learn.intro: EVs can feed power back to the grid, stabilizing supply during peaks. This transforms EVs into mobile energy storage units.
learn.c1_text: V2G allows EVs to discharge excess energy during demand spikes. A single EV can provide 5-10 kW during emergencies, reducing grid strain.
learn.c2_text: Bidirectional chargers enable energy flow from battery to grid. Smart algorithms optimize charging/discharging to avoid battery degradation.
learn.c3_text: India’s EV market aims for 30% penetration by 2030. Pilot projects in Delhi test V2G to support solar-rich grids during monsoon peaks.
learn.stat2: V2G can reduce peak demand by 15% in urban areas
learn.stat3: EV batteries retain 70-80% capacity after 8 years
learn.stat4: India’s FAME scheme includes V2G incentives for commercial fleets

learn.title: Bifacial Solar Panels
learn.intro: Bifacial panels capture sunlight on both sides, boosting efficiency by 10-20%. Ideal for reflective surfaces like rooftops or deserts.
learn.c1_text: Traditional panels use only front-facing light. Bifacial panels add rear-side gain, especially on white gravel or glass surfaces.
learn.c2_text: With 27% efficiency, bifacial panels outperform mono-facial (22%). A 1 MW farm generates 10-15% more energy annually.
learn.c3_text: India’s largest bifacial farm in Kurnool generates 60 MW. The government’s PLI scheme subsidizes bifacial modules to meet 2030 targets.
learn.stat4: India’s PLI scheme offers 20% subsidy for bifacial module manufacturing

learn.title: Battery Management Systems (BMS)
learn.intro: BMS protects batteries from overcharging, overheating, and wear, extending lifespan and ensuring safety in EVs and grids.
learn.c1_text: BMS monitors voltage, temperature, and state of charge. It prevents thermal runaway, reducing fire risks by 99% in lithium-ion systems.
learn.c2_text: Cell balancing ensures uniform charging. Advanced BMS uses AI to predict degradation, optimizing performance for 5-10 year lifespans.
learn.c3_text: Indian startups like Exponent Energy develop BMS for EVs, cutting costs by 30%. The government’s PLI scheme funds domestic BMS R&D.
learn.stat3: India’s PLI scheme targets 50 GWh domestic battery cell production by 2025
learn.stat4: BMS reduces EV battery replacement costs by 40%

learn.title: Wave Energy Converters
learn.intro: Wave energy harnesses ocean motion via buoys, oscillating systems, or turbines. It’s predictable and abundant but requires advanced tech.
learn.c1_text: Types include point absorbers (buoys), oscillating bodies, and overtopping systems. Each converts wave kinetic energy into electricity.
learn.c2_text: Oscillating water columns use air pressure changes to drive turbines. Efficiency ranges from 15-40%, depending on wave height and frequency.
learn.c3_text: India’s 7,000 km coastline has 120 GW wave potential. The National Institute of Ocean Technology is testing prototypes in Tamil Nadu.
learn.stat2: Wave energy density in India: 40-70 kW/m (2024)
learn.stat4: India’s National Policy on Marine Energy (2023) targets 1 GW by 2030
